title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
portfolio: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would refine National Disability Insurance Scheme rules, agency governance and participant safeguards, and make related changes to appeals, taxation and income support laws.
Scheme payments for funded supports would be exempt from income tax and excluded from social security and veterans' income and assets tests.
Before taking over or pursuing a participant's compensation claim, the chief executive would need to consider specified personal circumstances and give 28 days written notice.
changes: A dedicated scheme division would be established within the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.
An impairment affecting either social or economic participation could meet the relevant disability requirement.
Plan nominees who were insolvents under administration could remain appointed but could not manage plan funding.
The chief executive could appoint more than one plan nominee for a participant.
Mobility allowance would not be payable where a participant's scheme plan specified funded reasonable and necessary supports.
summary.affected: Scheme participants and prospective participants, nominees and support providers are affected.
